Endpoint paths are versioned per resource (/v3/, /v6/, checks-v2 etc.), but I found NO published deprecation/versioning policy page: /docs/rest-api/versioning is 404 and the overview has no versioning or deprecation prose. Evidence supports 'versioned APIs' only; the 'documented deprecation policy' half of the story remains undocumented. Judge decides; likely partial at best.

Vercel Observability now has user-emitted custom metrics plus Query, Monitoring and Notebooks sections in the docs nav. This covers custom metrics and querying/analysis inside Vercel; it does NOT show combining metrics from arbitrary external services into one dashboard, so the story is at most partially met. Marker 1 comes from the page's JSON-LD description, which survives the tag-strip verification.

This is a significant change from the old 'no Docker on Vercel' state: Vercel Functions now have a Container runtime built from a Dockerfile/Containerfile at the project root. Marker 1 is from the JSON-LD description (present in tag-stripped body). The prior partial verdict's rationale (Git push/CLI only, no Dockerfile) is outdated.

Marker 2 is a table row flattened by the tag-strip + whitespace-collapse procedure; verified verbatim against that exact transformation. Page description is 'Look up account limits, usage summaries, rate limits, and resource constraints for every Vercel plan.'

The historical 'Vercel Functions do not support WebSockets' position is no longer current: first-class inbound WebSocket support is documented, with framework guides (ws, Socket.IO, Bun, Nitro, FastAPI/ASGI, Django Channels, Flask-Sock). Caveat documented on the page: "WebSocket connections close when a Vercel Function reaches its maximum duration", so connections are bounded by the function duration limit and clients must reconnect.

Wall-clock (maximum duration) limits are explicit per plan. CPU-time is billed separately as Active CPU (see /docs/functions/usage-and-pricing); there is no separate CPU-time cutoff documented, duration is the binding limit. Markers are table rows flattened by tag-strip + whitespace collapse, verified against that transformation.

Exact per-unit on-demand (overage) rates for bandwidth, requests, compute, and memory are published. Markers are flattened table rows; verified against the tag-strip + whitespace-collapse transformation.

Checked 2026-11-03. The enterprise marketing page has zero mentions of 'migration' or 'credit'; the incremental-migration docs describe technical migration strategies only; pricing and Pro plan docs describe usage credits ($20/month Pro credit) but no migration/switching credits or onboarding discounts. Still absent.

Checked 2026-11-03. HTTP and now WebSocket traffic are served by Vercel Functions (see edge-websocket-support cell), but there is no documentation of inbound raw TCP, UDP, or native gRPC serving; the only TCP mention in functions limitations is outbound TCP sockets counting against the file-descriptor limit. The Container runtime docs describe HTTP port resolution, not arbitrary protocol listeners. The full multi-protocol story (HTTP+TCP+gRPC+WebSocket from one service) remains absent, though the WebSocket half is new evidence.
First-party object storage with server and client (browser) upload flows, SDKs, signed URLs, private/public stores. Marker 1 is from the JSON-LD description, present in tag-stripped body.

Checked 2026-11-03. No documented one-shot 'export all my data' feature. The REST API provides programmatic read access to deployments, projects, env vars, logs, etc., and Log Drains can stream logs out to S3/Datadog/Splunk, and the privacy notice documents individual privacy rights requests, but none of these is a documented full-account data export in open formats. Still absent as a product feature; judge may count REST API access as partial mitigation.

This names the previously-missing license for the CLI/builders repo: Apache-2.0. It covers the CLI, builders, and Build Output tooling (plus Next.js is MIT), NOT the hosted platform itself, which remains closed source. The prior partial verdict's gap ('pack never names a license for the CLI repo') is now evidenced. In the tag-stripped raw file, the license title whitespace collapses to 'Apache License Version 2.0, January 2004'.

Direct hit for the story: Active CPU billing pauses during I/O waits. Caveat for the judge: Provisioned Memory is a second dimension that IS billed for the entire instance lifetime (per GB-hr), so idle wall-clock is not entirely free, but CPU is billed active-time-only.

Region selection is documented for Blob stores and for function execution. This is region pinning for compute/storage rather than a formal data-residency compliance program (no residency guarantee page found for logs/metadata), so the judge may score partial.

A documented team-level opt-out of model training exists. Honesty caveat for the judge: the same notice says Vercel may use information to "train the AI models that support our Services" and may share de-identified AI Product Information with AI business partners for model training; the opt-out is a control, not a default no-training guarantee. /legal/privacy-policy 301-redirects to /legal/privacy-notice.

Partial: retention periods are plan-determined rather than user-configurable, and Log Drains extend rather than shorten retention. Account-level data deletion exists via privacy rights in the privacy notice. No configurable retention/deletion knobs for logs or traces are documented, so the judge will likely score partial. /docs/observability/logs 308-redirects to /docs/logs.
Documented opt-out covers Vercel CLI telemetry (command + env var + status check). It does not cover dashboard/product analytics, so scope is the developer tooling.

Important for the repair script: the HTML pages at vercel-status.com/ and /history render incident content via JS (curl body is mostly CSS), so markers must be verified against history.rss (server-rendered XML; tag-strip leaves titles and entity-encoded update text) or an individual incident page title. The RSS feed rotates as new incidents occur, so the two markers chosen are the durable ones (feed title and the incidents URL prefix). Incident updates are status timelines, not deep postmortems.

Published 99.99% uptime SLA with defined downtime credits; applies to Enterprise ('Enterprise Service Level Agreement'). Quoted terms in the source are wrapped in " entities, so markers avoid crossing quote boundaries.

Redis is available via Vercel Marketplace native integrations (e.g. Upstash), with provisioning and env-var injection handled by Vercel; the first-party Vercel KV product was retired. Judge decides whether marketplace-native counts as built-in; evidence is vendor-official.

Region selection per project and per function is documented, including multi-region (Pro/Enterprise) and failover regions; the fluid compute pricing page lists ~19 selectable regions with per-region rates. Static assets remain served from the global CDN regardless.

Per-seat pricing is fully documented: minimum 1 paid deploying seat on Pro, $20/month per additional Owner/Member seat, unlimited free viewer seats (so cost scales with deploying members only). Marker 2 preserves the page's literal spacing '$ 20 /month each' after tag-strip; do not normalize it.

Confirms the existing partial: serverless Postgres comes via Marketplace native integrations (Neon etc.), provisioned and credential-injected by Vercel, but the first-party Vercel Postgres product (and its SDK) was retired; no first-party no-connection-management driver is documented on this page. Judge likely keeps partial.

Weak/partial evidence: the Build Output API is an open, documented deployment spec, and current Vercel Functions run standard servers (Express, Hono, FastAPI, Bun, standard Node.js http) rather than requiring proprietary handler signatures, which reduces lock-in. But no Vercel page claims code runs unmodified on other edge platforms, and storage/products (Blob, etc.) remain proprietary APIs. Judge decides; probably partial at most.

Published per-severity target response times exist, but only for Enterprise support tiers (Standard/Premium) and framed as targets ('We only commit to respond to Customers with an Enterprise subscription'). The '<' signs in the severity table are < entities in the source, so markers avoid them. /docs/support redirects to /docs/support-center, which covers ticketing mechanics only.
